clue.text: Came across a number employed in steel-works

parts.note: to come across someone is to have met them
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a number

explanation.surface: Someone stumbled on a figure for the headcount at a steel plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: what is used in steelworks is the raw material poured and rolled there.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron and other such elements are the material processed and used in a steel mill.

definitions.meaning: the police seizing an offender, the first step against a criminal

explanation.surface: Halt a prosecution in its tracks?
explanation.definitionFit: To halt is the general sense; the police detention of a suspect is the legal sense that starts criminal proceedings.

parts.note: read as losing one's head, the top part or leader of the body, by execution

explanation.surface: An order to assassinate a chief.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'leader' is also the head on one's shoulders; losing it by the axe is the fate described.
explanation.definitionFit: Execution by axe removes the head, which is the body's leading part.

clue.text: Writer comes up with a melody for deep character

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a pen is something you write with
a tune is a melody

explanation.surface: An author arrives bearing a song for a profound personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deep' is the sea: the Roman sea god is the character meant, not a thoughtful person.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of the sea is a mythological figure of the ocean depths.

parts.note: to rid is to free of something
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Clearing results from a loose ball in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free ball' suggests a sports situation; it is RID (free) plus DANCE (ball).
explanation.definitionFit: Getting rid of something unwanted is a clearing out of it.

clue.text: Journalist's work needs to be bang on time

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another comes above it, so it is written first

parts.note: a report is a loud bang, as of a gun
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A reporter's piece has to be exactly punctual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bang on time' reads as 'exactly punctual', but 'bang' is a gunshot's noise and 'on' places one piece above the other in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Reporting of news events by the press is the work journalists produce.

clue.text: He has the skill and might need to be encouraged

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of conversation

indicators.note: might suggests the letters of the word need could be rearranged into a possible new form

explanation.surface: A capable man may still need some cheering up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' looks like a verb of possibility, but it signals that the following word is rearranged; 'has the' and 'to be' are only link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Being heartened is being given courage or hope, cheered up.

definitions.meaning: a handball-like court game played at some English schools
in Britain children start school at five years old

explanation.surface: A playground game suited to the youngest pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: The court game is played with gloved hands; five-year-olds are the age at which British children begin school.

clue.text: Quiet morning? Don't you believe it

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
am stands for the morning hours

explanation.surface: A peaceful morning? You must be joking.
explanation.definitionFit: A fake or pretence is something not to be believed.

clue.text: Equestrian ability acquired by large majority

definitions.text: Equestrian ability acquired by large majority

parts.words: Equestrian ability acquired by large majority
parts.note: a secure seat on a horse is riding skill; a big electoral majority gives an MP a constituency they cannot lose

explanation.surface: Most riders manage to learn to ride well.
explanation.walkthrough: A rider's 'seat' is their position and balance in the saddle; in British politics a constituency held by a large majority is a secure one.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliamentary constituency won by a big margin is one the holder cannot easily lose.

parts.note: a bay is both the howl of hunting dogs and a sea inlet; this Canadian inlet's name sounds like a dog's son

explanation.surface: The baying of a pack of hunting dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: The bay in northern Canada named after the explorer Henry; 'hounds' plays on 'Hud son' as a dog's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The large Canadian sea inlet is named after the English explorer Henry of that surname.

parts.note: a boss is a raised knob or ornament, and an outstanding one literally stands out from a surface

explanation.surface: A brilliant manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' is a projecting knob, not a manager; 'outstanding' means sticking out.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised knob or rivet head projecting from a surface is a decorative boss.

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of mention and a are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Bring up a fresh name.
explanation.definitionFit: To name someone for a post is to put them forward as a candidate.

clue.text: Sweetheart to approve a new tie

parts.note: to favour something is to approve of it

indicators.note: new says the letters of tie are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A loved one approves of a recently bought necktie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tie' reads as a necktie; 'new' signals its letters are shuffled to follow the verb meaning approve.
explanation.definitionFit: A darling or best-loved person is the one most preferred.

indicators.note: in places the rotter inside the law-suit

parts.note: a case is a lawsuit in court
a cad is a rotter, an ungentlemanly man

explanation.surface: The downfall of a scoundrel caught up in litigation.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterfall tumbling in stages is a fall of water.

clue.text: Lois came out in her underwear

indicators.note: came out suggests the letters emerge in a different order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Lois appeared wearing only her lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Came out' looks like a phrase about Lois appearing; 'came' is fodder and 'out' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A light sleeveless top worn beneath clothing is women's lingerie.

parts.note: under means less than, as in under ten pounds
go is energy or vigour

explanation.surface: Going through a time of reduced vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: To go through or suffer something is to experience it.

parts.note: the Grand steeplechase at Aintree is a great event held on a racecourse

explanation.surface: A splendid event, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is Britain's most famous horse race, run at Aintree; 'of course' means on a racecourse, not 'naturally'.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous steeplechase is called the Grand one, run each spring at Aintree racecourse.

clue.text: They took over from the night-shift

definitions.text: They took over from the night-shift

parts.words: They took over from the night-shift
parts.note: a nightshirt was the old sleeping garment, and the two-piece sleeping suit replaced it

explanation.surface: Day workers relieving the overnight team.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'night-shift' is a nightshirt or nightdress, not a work rota.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-piece sleeping suit replaced the long nightshirt as bedtime wear.

parts.note: a form is a school class
an ally is a friend or mate

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone is a classmate, then agreeing exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in the correct official way is doing it precisely by the rules.

definitions.meaning: advanced as in ... money, supplied on loan
the Christian season of fasting before Easter, when people give things up

explanation.surface: Moved forward the date for an offering.
explanation.definitionFit: Advancing money is a loan given; the forty days before Easter are when Christians give up luxuries.

clue.text: It has branches in every street

indicators.note: in every means the word street carries the answer inside it

explanation.surface: Something leafy lines every road.
explanation.walkthrough: An &lit flavour: trees really do line streets, and one sits inside the word 'street'.
explanation.definitionFit: An oak or elm grows boughs off its trunk.

parts.note: E is a musical key
the state is the public body, as in state schools

explanation.surface: The secret to owning land held in common.
explanation.definitionFit: Land and buildings owned by one person or body are their holdings.

definitions.meaning: the smallest cathedral city in England, in Somerset
shafts sunk to draw water from underground

explanation.surface: A town's reservoirs.
explanation.walkthrough: WELLS is a small English cathedral city in Somerset.
explanation.definitionFit: The Somerset cathedral city takes its name from springs; boreholes provide groundwater.

clue.text: Is in a porn production, gets jail

indicators.note: a production is something made up, so the letters of is and porn are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone who acts in an adult film ends up locked away.
explanation.definitionFit: A jail is a lockup where convicts are held.

parts.note: Acts is the New Testament book recording what Christ's twelve followers did

explanation.surface: Performers whose routines are famous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acts' looks like stage turns; it is the Bible's Acts of the Apostles.
explanation.definitionFit: The twelve disciples' deeds are told in the New Testament book of Acts.

definitions.meaning: a retort is a distilling vessel, as is this apparatus for making spirits

explanation.surface: A cool reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retort' is the chemist's distilling flask, not a sharp reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Motionless water is calm; the distillery apparatus is like a chemist's retort.

indicators.note: spinning sets the letters of natural at whirling into a new order, fitting a web-spinner

explanation.surface: A spider is a natural at weaving webs.
explanation.definitionFit: The large hairy arachnid is a well-known kind of spider.
